body.statement: Given a finite first-order formula in the language of ordered rings whose atomic predicates are polynomial equalities or inequalities with rational coefficients, cylindrical algebraic decomposition terminates, constructs finitely many sign-invariant cells with exact real-algebraic sample-point data, and decides the formula.  In particular, existential projections of rational semialgebraic sets are semialgebraic and are computable by quantifier elimination; the general projection-and-lifting procedure can have doubly exponential worst-case growth in the number of variables.
